summary: Fold each mission detail step's attempts, waits and transitions, estimate each remaining step, lift the detail bound for a requested run, and show a mission revision's recorded source

replay.detail: No claim replay or recovery behavior changes. The step history is folded at read time from durable step-run and work claims the store already holds; nothing is written.

schema.detail: No tables, indexes, triggers, schema-version changes or data rewrites. The detail read adds one batched read of the enriched runs' step lifecycle claims, without lease renewals; per-step ETA reads the existing local_run_eta_samples rows.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rules, retention classes or digest changes; no coordinated member upgrade required.

compatibility.detail: Additive optional fields on GET /v1/client/missions/{id} only: run_details[].steps[].attempts, waits, transitions, history_complete and eta; and optional provenance {repository, commit, path, renderer} on GET /v1/client/mission-declaration. GET /v1/client/missions/{id} accepts an optional ?run=<mission run id> that lifts its timing and enrichment bound for that run (a run of another mission is 404; older daemons ignore the query); the TypeScript, Rust and Swift clients send it through a new missionsGetRun(id, run) / missions_get_run method, leaving missionsGet unchanged. Lists, pages and collection windows are unchanged. New outcome, wait-kind and event words are open enums. Roll out daemons before clients; clients read the fields' absence from an older daemon as unknown.

downtime.detail: No startup work. A detail read folds the lifecycle claims of its open runs, latest finished run and requested run, capped at 20 attempts, 40 waits and 60 transitions per step.

recovery.detail: Swapping back to an older daemon only drops the new optional fields and ignores ?run=. No persistent state changes.
